page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The hardware configuration features 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processors running at 2.0 GHz, with a shared CPU allocation model and one thread per core. It includes 960.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered by four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, which supply a combined 320 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, meaning external storage volumes must be attached.

Benchmark data shows strong multi-core CPU and memory performance. The server achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 96293.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 85426.66, both placing in the top 25%. Extended instruction tests reached 117918.35, placing in the top 10%, aided by hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory bandwidth is a notable highlight, with small-block cached read speeds reaching 7649.82 GB/sec and large-block uncached read speeds at 316.04 GB/sec. Large-language model inference benchmarks using a 135M model demonstrated prompt processing speeds of 10308.98 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 377.14 tokens per second, both ranking in the top 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents a dense, high-tier resource allocation where the cost is heavily weighted toward the four enterprise-grade NVIDIA H100 GPUs and the massive 960 GB memory footprint. A key tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the lack of local storage, which requires users to factor in network-attached storage performance. This configuration is designed for workloads such as large-scale machine learning, LLM inference, data science pipelines, and complex physical simulations.
